CAUSE: I can't see your repository, so I haven't confirmed this is what happened to it. The most likely cause is that `main` already contains the worker's change, so `git merge --squash` stages nothing and no commit is made. In `merge_worktree_to_main`, an empty squash is reported as `NO_COMMITS_MERGED`. The code does not treat it as "already merged". The wording "merge produced no new commits" fits this, but other causes could produce the same message.

EVIDENCE
- `app/workspace.py`, `merge_worktree_to_main` (about lines 1608–1675): it runs `git merge --squash <worker_head>` in the target checkout. It then runs `git diff --cached --quiet`. If that shows nothing staged, it returns `{"ok": True, "commits_merged": 0}` and makes no commit.
- Same function, about lines 1723–1732: `ok` is true but `target_after == target_before`. It sets `code = NO_COMMITS_MERGED`, `error = "merge produced no new commits"`, `state = failed` and `commit_point = not_reached`.
- `app/merge_operations.py`, `_classify_failure` and the check around line 1020, plus `app/routes/sessions.py` around line 2105: these apply the same rule (`target_before == target_after` and `commits_merged == 0`). They then show the generic `CHECK_WORKER_THEN_NEW_OPERATION` text you received.
- Other branches don't produce this message. If `main` and the worker point to the same commit, the error is "point to the same commit; refusing…". Conflicts, a dirty tree and a moved target each have their own code.

REPRODUCTION
- I ran `workspace.merge_worktree_to_main` on throwaway repos in `scratch/`. The scripts are `scratch/repro.py` and `scratch/repro2.py`.
- Normal case: a linked worktree on `task-416/worker` adds a new `worker.txt`. The merge succeeded and `main` moved.
- Same-content case: `main` already had an identical `worker.txt` before the merge. The result was `ok=False`, `code=NO_COMMITS_MERGED`, `error="merge produced no new commits"`, `commits_merged=0`, `state=failed`. `main` didn't move. `git log main..worker` would still list the commit, because it is a different commit with the same tree change.
- I only tested this one cause. I did not try other ways to get an empty squash.

HOW TO CONFIRM ON THE REAL REPO
- Run `git cat-file -p main:worker.txt` and `git cat-file -p task-416/worker:worker.txt`. If `main` already has the file with identical content, this is the cause.
- Run `git diff main...task-416/worker --stat`. If it is empty, nothing is left to merge.
- Find how the content got into `main` with `git log main -- worker.txt`. It may have been committed directly, merged earlier from another branch, or cherry-picked.

FIX
- If the content is already in `main`, nothing needs merging. Mark the task as already delivered, or reset the worker branch to `main`. Don't retry the merge, because it will give the same result.
- If the content is not in `main`, this cause is wrong. Then check `git config`, `.git/info/attributes` and any sparse-checkout setup in the main checkout. Also look for environment variables such as `GIT_DIR` or `GIT_WORK_TREE` in the process that runs the merge.
- Code improvement: when the squash is empty and `git diff <target> <worker_head>` is empty, return a distinct code such as `ALREADY_MERGED` or `NO_CHANGES`. At the moment this case looks like a failure and tells the orchestrator to retry.
